summary: Build practical ESG and human-rights due-diligence skills for supplier screening, engagement, auditing, and reporting. Explore the five-day course.
lede: ESG and human rights due diligence training helps procurement, compliance, category, and sustainability professionals turn responsible-business principles into practical supplier decisions and contract controls. You will learn to identify, prevent, mitigate, track, and communicate risks including forced labour, child labour, unsafe working conditions, discrimination, environmental harm, and corruption. The course covers supplier risk registers, multi-tier mapping, screening, leverage assessment, audit evidence, corrective-action planning, grievance referral, remediation tracking, and leadership reporting. Practical templates and an implementation roadmap support integration into sourcing, contracting, supplier performance reviews, and executive reporting.
audienceIntro: ESG due diligence training suits professionals who make, control, monitor, or report supply-chain decisions across formal and informal supplier networks. It is designed for beginner to intermediate practitioners who understand procurement or sustainability operations and need a structured implementation approach.
prerequisites: You should have working exposure to procurement, supplier management, compliance, sustainability, logistics, or supply-chain risk. No legal qualification, audit certification, or programming experience is required. Bring a representative supplier category, sourcing process, or anonymized risk scenario if available. Advanced technology content remains at operational application level, with AI-assisted screening introduced for controlled use rather than technical model development.
